title: Coefficient changes commute with $\eta_f$
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of condensed abelian groups, i.e. sheaves of abelian groups on profinite sets with the coherent topology, and let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. For $T=X,Y$, let $p_T^*$ be the inverse image from the point of [def-sfb-upper-star-from-point], and put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, $\Lambda'_T=p_T^*\Lambda'$ and $a_T=p_T^*a$. Let $f^*$ and $f_*$ be the pullback and pushforward of abelian pro-étale sheaves of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] and [def-sfb-finite-lower-star], with adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] and unit $u\colon\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$. Write $c_f\colon f^*p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ for the natural isomorphism of [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso], and define
$$
\alpha_f=(c_f)_\Lambda,\qquad \alpha'_f=(c_f)_{\Lambda'},\qquad
\eta_f=f_*\alpha_f\circ u_{\Lambda_Y},\qquad
\eta'_f=f_*\alpha'_f\circ u_{\Lambda'_Y}.
$$
When $\Lambda$, $\Lambda'$ are condensed rings and $a$ is a ring morphism, these are exactly the underlying abelian-sheaf constructions of [def-sfb-coefficient-map] and [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Then
$$
f_*a_X\circ\eta_f=\eta'_f\circ a_Y\colon\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow f_*\Lambda'_X.
$$

proof.text:
The current definition [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso] explicitly constructs $c_f$ on abelian pro-étale sheaves by precomposing the inverse pullback-composition isomorphism with $p^*$, followed by the identification from $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$. It states that this composite is a natural isomorphism on all condensed abelian groups. Thus its naturality equation at $a$ is
$$
\alpha'_f\circ f^*(p_Y^*a)=p_X^*a\circ\alpha_f.
$$
Substituting $a_Y=p_Y^*a$ and $a_X=p_X^*a$ gives $\alpha'_f\circ f^*a_Y=a_X\circ\alpha_f$, an equality from $f^*\Lambda_Y$ to $\Lambda'_X$. This expands the blueprint's pullback-square step using the stated naturality of the current comparison; no ring structure is required.

source.place: Complete proof: naturality of the coefficient comparison, then naturality of the adjunction unit

proof.text:
The unit $u$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] is a natural transformation $\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^*$, so its defining naturality equation at $a_Y$ is $f_*f^*a_Y\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}=u_{\Lambda'_Y}\circ a_Y$. Expand the two mates using the formulas in the statement, use functoriality of $f_*$ and the preceding step, then this naturality equation:
$$
\begin{aligned}
f_*a_X\circ\eta_f
&=f_*(a_X\circ\alpha_f)\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}\\
&=f_*\alpha'_f\circ f_*f^*a_Y\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}\\
&=f_*\alpha'_f\circ u_{\Lambda'_Y}\circ a_Y
=\eta'_f\circ a_Y.
\end{aligned}
$$
Every composite has source $\Lambda_Y$ and target $f_*\Lambda'_X$. Only the definitions of natural transformation and functor, and associativity of composition, enter this calculation.

source.place: Complete proof: naturality of the coefficient comparison, then naturality of the adjunction unit

proof.text:
For the ring specialization, [def-sfb-coefficient-map] defines $a_T=p_T^*a$ for $T=X,Y$. To compare the two named comparisons, use their explicit construction in [def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp-iso] and [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. Write $d\colon(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*\pi_Y^*$ for the composition isomorphism appearing in both definitions, and $e\colon(\pi_Y\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_X^*$ for their identification using $\pi_Y\circ f=\pi_X$. For every condensed abelian group $H$, both underlying comparisons have component
$$
e_{p^*H}\circ d^{-1}_{p^*H}\colon f^*\pi_Y^*p^*H\longrightarrow\pi_X^*p^*H.
$$
In particular they agree at $H=\Lambda$ and $H=\Lambda'$, by substitution of the definitions, independently of the monoidal structures. Now [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] defines $\alpha_f$ as that component at $\Lambda$, and $\eta_f$ as the adjunction unit followed by $f_*\alpha_f$. Hence its underlying maps are exactly $(c_f)_\Lambda$ and $f_*((c_f)_\Lambda)\circ u_{\Lambda_Y}$, and likewise for $\Lambda'$. This proves the conditional identification in the statement. The equality from step 2 already holds for every condensed abelian-group morphism, including those without ring structures.

    condensedPushforwardHom Λ f ≫ (f)_*[Ab.{u + 1}].map (coefficientMap a X) =
      coefficientMap a Y ≫ condensedPushforwardHom Λ' f
